title: Driving a sandpoint well with a pitcher pump
summary: Where the water table is within about 6 m of the surface in sand or gravel, a steel pipe with a screened point can be driven by hand and topped with a pitcher pump. Shallow water is easily polluted, so site it well away and uphill from septic fields and barnyards, seal it at the surface, disinfect and test it. The dangers are mashed hands at the drive cap, buried cables, and drinking untested water.

materials.item: Drive well point with stainless screen, 32 mm (1 1/4 in) or 50 mm (2 in)
Steel or galvanised pipe in 1.2–1.8 m lengths, same size as the point
materials.qty: depth to water, plus the screen, plus about 60 cm to spare below the water table, plus about 90 cm above ground for the pump

materials.item: Drop pipe to hang inside the well pipe, narrower than it so it fits, and long enough to end at least 1.5 m (5 ft) under water
Foot valve, only if you can keep the pump from freezing
Clay soil, to seal round the pipe

steps.text: Check the ground and the water: sand or gravel, no rock near the surface, and the water table within about 6 m (20 ft) at its lowest (Wisconsin DG-022). Neighbours' wells and well records tell you most of this.

Pick the spot: high ground, uphill from and at least 30 m (100 ft) from any septic field or latrine and 100 m from manure storage, out of flood-prone ground, not in a basement or pit (Manitoba well fact sheet; Wisconsin DG-022).
steps.warn: Get buried lines located before you drive anything: ask for a free locate and allow about 5 business days. It skips private lines, such as gas to a barbecue or power to a shed (Ontario Dig Authority homeowners; Boshart well points).

steps.text: Screw a drive coupling and the first pipe onto the point. Rub a bar of soap over the screen to keep clay out and ease driving. Put the drive cap on top, with no thread compound on it (UMN wellpoint).

Dig or auger a starter hole 2.5 to 5 cm (1 to 2 in) wider than the point and as deep as you can (UMN wellpoint). Frozen ground will probably make this much harder, so drive before freeze-up if you can.
Stand the pipe plumb with a level and drive it with square, solid blows on the cap only (UMN wellpoint; Merrill FAQ).
steps.warn: A glancing blow or a post driver coming off the top crushes hands. Keep hands off the cap while someone else strikes; wear gloves, eye protection and ear protection (steel on steel is loud).

steps.text: When the cap is about 10 cm (4 in) above ground, take it off, add the next coupling and pipe, and tighten with two wrenches turning against each other so you don't twist the string underground. Give the pipe an occasional half turn to keep joints tight (UMN wellpoint).

Every so often pour water in. When about 4 L (1 US gal) disappears within 2 minutes you are in water-bearing sand (UMN wellpoint). Keep going until the whole screen is below the water table with about 60 cm (2 ft) to spare for dry seasons (Boshart well points).
Develop the well: surge a rod or closed pipe up and down just below the water level for about 5 minutes, then pump out the sand; repeat until it pumps clear (UMN wellpoint).
Fill the gap around the pipe with very wet, puddled clay and mound it so surface water runs away (UMN wellpoint). Leave the pipe at least 40 cm (16 in) above the ground (EFP water wells).

Hang a drop pipe inside the well pipe down into the water, seal the threads airtight, and mount the pitcher pump about 90 cm (3 ft) above ground (UMN wellpoint). The pump maker wants the bottom of the drop pipe at least 1.5 m (5 ft) under water (Water Source pitcher pump).

Prime with clean water: fill the pump until it runs out of the spout, wait 7 to 10 minutes for the leather to swell, then pump with short strokes (Boshart Model 19). Keep a hand on the handle: it can fly up if you let go on the downstroke (Boshart Model 19).

Disinfect: 1 cup (about 250 mL) of 5.25 % bleach in about 3 L of water down the pipe, wait 12 hours, then pump until the chlorine smell is gone (UMN wellpoint). Test for coliforms and nitrate before drinking (Wisconsin DG-022).
steps.warn: Never mix the bleach with vinegar, acids or cleaners.

steps.text: Before frost, leave the handle all the way up after each use so the pump drains, or take the pump off if it has a foot valve (Boshart Model 19; Water Source pitcher pump).

notes:
## Will it work here?
A sandpoint (driven point) well is steel pipe, 32 or 50 mm (1 1/4 or 2 in) across, with a 60 to 90 cm (2 to 3 ft) screen and a hardened tip on the bottom, driven into the ground in sections until the screen sits in water-bearing sand (Wisconsin DG-022). It needs two things:
- **Sand or gravel you can drive through.** Boulders, hardpan and clay stop the point, and clay holds water but won't give it up to a well (Wisconsin DG-022). Coarse sand drives most easily and fine sand is hardest; sharp gravel tears the screen (Boshart well points). Avoid compacted rock and solid stone layers (Merrill FAQ).
- **A shallow water table.** A suction pump at the top doesn't pull water up; air pressure pushes it, and that only goes so far (Wisconsin DG-022).

| Source | How high a suction pump lifts |
|---|---|
| Practica rope pump manual, about suction pumps in general | 10 m in theory, 6 to 7 m in practice |
| Wisconsin DG-022 | about 6 m (20 ft) for a shallow-well pump |
| Boshart Model 19 | about 6 m (20 ft) at sea level for its pitcher pump (its intro says 7.6 m (25 ft) once, but the operating section and troubleshooting say 20 ft); take off 30 cm (1 ft) for every 300 m (1,000 ft) of elevation and for every 15 m (50 ft) of sideways pipe |
| Merrill FAQ; Bison FAQ; Water Source pitcher pump | 7.6 m (25 ft) maximum for their pitcher pumps; Water Source says that is at sea level in ideal conditions, and less higher up |

Plan on about 6 m (20 ft) from the **lowest** water level of the year to the pump. The water drops while you pump, and seasonally (Boshart well points). If it's deeper, you need a 50 mm (2 in) pipe with a jet assembly down the well and a powered pump (Wisconsin DG-022), or a different well.

Hand-driven points usually reach about 9 m (30 ft); heavier driving equipment can go to 15 m (50 ft) in ideal ground (Illinois driven wells). Look at neighbours' wells and well records for how deep the water is.

## Where to put it
Shallow water in sand is easily polluted by septic fields, manure and fertiliser (Wisconsin DG-022; UMN wellpoint), and sandpoints in New Brunswick are described as very vulnerable to contamination (GNB wells). Ontario's farm-plan guide says wells less than 3 m (10 ft) deep shouldn't be used at all (EFP water wells).

- On the highest ground you can, not downhill from a septic field, barnyard or fuel tank, out of any floodplain, and not in a basement or pit (Wisconsin DG-022; EFP water wells).
- Manitoba's setbacks: at least 8 m (26 ft) from a septic tank, 15 m (50 ft) from a septic field for a well drilled and cased to at least 6 m (20 ft) and 30 m (100 ft) for any other well (use 30 m for a driven point, which isn't drilled), and 100 m (330 ft) from manure storage and compost sites; 30 m from other contamination sources is good practice, and more in sand and gravel or for a shallow well (Manitoba well fact sheet). Latrine distances are in [Sanitation](#ref/reference_sanitation/latrines_and_distances).
- Wisconsin, where sandpoints are common, asks for at least 7.6 m (25 ft) from a septic tank or pond, 15 m (50 ft) from a septic field or animal yard, and 30 m (100 ft) from a buried petroleum tank (Wisconsin DG-022). Where in doubt, use the larger figure.
- Get buried lines located before you drive. Ontario's locate service is free, marks public utilities and asks for at least 5 business days' notice (look for your province's equivalent elsewhere). It does not mark private lines such as gas to a barbecue or pool heater, power to a shed or garage, or septic and sewer pipes (Ontario Dig Authority homeowners). Boshart's advice is to check with the utility so you don't put the well over underground service lines (Boshart well points). With no locate service running, stay clear of the ground between the street, the meter or pole and every building, and of any run towards a shed, pool or barbecue, and keep the pipe well away from overhead wires.

In Ontario and New Brunswick new wells are built by licensed well contractors (EFP water wells; GNB wells); in Wisconsin anyone may drive a point (Wisconsin DG-022). If there's no one to call, build it to the same standard anyway: that's what keeps the water clean.

## Parts
- **Point:** Merrill makes 32 and 50 mm (1 1/4 and 2 in) points with a cast-iron tip and stainless screen (Merrill FAQ). Screen openings come as mesh (40 to 80) or slots (7 to 18 thousandths of an inch): the right size lets the finest sand through and holds the coarser sand around the screen (UMN wellpoint). Wisconsin doesn't allow screens with more than 8 % lead, or plastic screens for driving, and recommends continuous-slot stainless (Wisconsin DG-022): so if you salvage an old brass point, assume it may hold lead. Health Canada says brass faucets and fittings may contain lead (Health Canada lead), so treat old brass pump parts and fittings the same way and prefer fittings certified to the low-lead standard. See [Lead](#browse/hazards/lead).
- **Pipe:** steel or galvanised steel, at least schedule 40, in 1.2 to 1.8 m (4 to 6 ft) lengths for hand driving (UMN wellpoint; Illinois driven wells).
- **Drive couplings** let the pipe ends butt together so the blows go through the pipe, not the threads; ordinary couplings can crack (UMN wellpoint).
- **Drive cap** on top while driving: it takes the blows and protects the threads (UMN wellpoint). Never hammer the pipe threads themselves (Merrill FAQ).
- **Driver:** a sledge, or a post driver (a short heavy pipe with handles), or a weight on a tripod and pulley for deeper wells (Wisconsin DG-022).

## Developing the well
New points are muddy and slow until the finest sand around the screen is pulled out, leaving a coarse, open layer that water flows through easily (UMN wellpoint). Surge it: work a wooden rod or closed pipe rapidly up and down just below the water level for about 5 minutes, then pump the sand out with the pitcher pump. Or run a garden hose to the bottom and let the water wash the sand up around it. Repeat until pumping brings up no more sand (UMN wellpoint).

## The pump and frost
- Put a drop pipe inside the well pipe, down into the water, and hang the pump from that. Then the pipe in contact with the soil is never under suction, so a leaky joint can't pull dirty water in (UMN wellpoint).
- A pitcher pump sits about 90 cm (3 ft) above ground; an electric pump with the pipe 30 cm (1 ft) or less above (UMN wellpoint).
- A pitcher pump with no foot valve drains itself when you leave the handle all the way up, which tips its check valve open (Boshart Model 19; Water Source pitcher pump). With a foot valve the pipe stays full, so the pump must come off in freezing weather, or be inside an insulated enclosure (Water Source pitcher pump; Wisconsin DG-022). Wisconsin also shows a hand pump protected from frost by an outer casing and a drain-back (Wisconsin DG-022). Leathers frozen to the pump body tear if you pump them (Water Source pitcher pump): thaw first.
- Care, priming and new leathers: [Hand and pitcher pumps](#guides/repair_hand_pump).

## Before you drink it
Disinfect a new well and flush it before use (Wisconsin DG-022). For a 32 to 50 mm well, the Minnesota guide used 1 cup (about 250 mL) of 5.25 % bleach in 3 quarts (about 3 L) of water poured in, left 12 hours, then pumped until the chlorine smell was gone (UMN wellpoint); the full method is in [Shock-chlorinating a well](#guides/skill_shock_chlorinate_well). Test for coliform bacteria and nitrate (Wisconsin DG-022), then test shallow wells regularly (UMN wellpoint). Until the bacteria test is clean, boil the water or treat it with chlorine: [Testing water](#guides/test_water). Neither removes nitrate, which comes from septic systems and fertiliser: Health Canada's limit is 45 mg/L, set to protect bottle-fed babies, and it says boiling won't reduce nitrate or nitrite and that water over the limit shouldn't be used to make formula (Health Canada nitrate). Shallow wells in farming areas are the most exposed (Health Canada nitrate). Fuel and other chemicals also survive boiling and chlorine: see [Shock-chlorinating a well](#guides/skill_shock_chlorinate_well).
